newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expects Eurobond rating by Oct 10 - official.
newsitem.headline: Russia expects Eurobond rating by Oct 10 - official.

text.p: Russia expects to hear what credit rating it has been allocated for its forthcoming Eurobond by October 10, a top finance ministry official said on Thursday.
First Deputy Finance Minister Andrei Vavilov told a news conference the Russian authorities had worked with three rating agencies this month to produce a rating.
"It looks like they will draw up the rating...at the beginning of October and by October 10, we will find out what kind of rating we will get," he said.
Vavilov declined to name the agencies involved, but Western bankers said Standard & Poors was here last week.
Western bankers said they expected Russia to receive a rating in the range of BBB to BB-, just above or below investment grade. Nevertheless, the Eurobond was expected to attract great interest.

Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said last week Russia would launch the Eurobond at the end of October or early November. Officials said the first issue will have a volume of $300-500 million.

Kasyanov said commecial banks have agreed in principle to reschedule $20 billion of Russian debt inherited from the former Soviet Union, clearing the way for a rescheduling of all the $35 billion still owed banks. This global rescheduling was seen as a precondition of getting a good rating.
